findings.title: The detach evicts the map key without an identity check, so a stale detach could evict a NEWER attachment's Set
findings.code: const detach = (): void => { attached.delete(detach); if (attached.size === 0) this.liveByParticipant.delete(participantId); unsubscribe(); };
findings.mechanism: The closure captures `attached` (the Set that existed at attach time) but deletes the map entry by KEY. After a drain (:704-705) the key is gone; if a later attachment for the same participantId installed a NEW Set under that key, the original detach - which production still calls on socket close, the double-call the design explicitly anticipates - would run `this.liveByParticipant.delete(participantId)` and evict the new Set WITHOUT unsubscribing it. That attachment would keep delivering while becoming invisible to any future drain: the exact leak this fix exists to close.
findings.reachabilityVerdict: NOT REACHABLE in the current tree, verified rather than assumed
findings.whyNotReachable: A re-attachment for a drained participant is the precondition, and it cannot happen: every campaign-scoped sink is created inside handleCampaignJoin (bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:898-1186) and that function refuses a revoked participant at :934-939 before every attach arm; the heal pass (:407-410, :873-879) re-applies the removal on each later authenticated frame; there is no ParticipantAdded/re-grant intent (grep of CampaignMatchHostIntent.ts shows only mk('ParticipantRemoved', ...) at :228); and a single socket's cleanup cannot fire twice (the `cleanedUp` guard at bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:254-257).
findings.recommendation: OPTIONAL one-line hardening, not required for this merge: `if (this.liveByParticipant.get(participantId) === attached && attached.size === 0) this.liveByParticipant.delete(participantId);`. It makes the detach safe under identity rather than safe under a distant invariant in another file. If the revocation-refusal gate at :934 is ever relaxed (for example to let a re-invited member back into the same session), this becomes live and should be applied in that change.
findings.note: This finding and mutant c point in opposite directions: mutant c removes the self-deregistration and therefore also removes this eviction side effect. The deregistration is still the right call (it stops unbounded map growth across reconnects); the guard is what makes keeping it free of this edge.

axis7_revocationCellJudgement.question: Does silencing the revoked socket, without a typed close, satisfy the R2.authority-live 'revocation' cell, or must the cell stay partial?
axis7_revocationCellJudgement.cellText: roadmap.json, node R2.authority-live, acceptance[4]: 'Real isolated source and replica processes, append/restart/catch-up/revocation/redaction; reviewed migration states/parity/rollback before enabling journal authority'
axis7_revocationCellJudgement.judgement: SATISFIED for the campaign-scoped live surface. The cell should NOT be held partial on the typed close.
reasoning: The acceptance element is 'revocation' inside a two-process live drive, not 'revocation is announced to the revoked client'. The substantive question is whether a revoked seat can still OBSERVE campaign state, and after this fix it cannot.

The closure is now total across the three doors, each measured: the already-bound live socket is drained (e2e row R3, green on my own run this session); the scoped read in the OTHER process is refused (pre-existing row in the same spec, still green); a rejoin is refused by name with AUTH_REJECTED 'membership-revoked' (bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:934-939).

There is no re-acquisition path: every campaign-scoped sink creation site sits inside handleCampaignJoin behind that refusal (verified in axis 1), so the revoked socket cannot re-subscribe by sending a resync or rejoin frame on the connection it still holds.

What remains absent is client FEEDBACK, not authority: the removed player's screen goes quiet rather than telling them why. That is a UX defect, and a real one - a silent socket is indistinguishable from an idle campaign - but it cannot leak a fact, and holding an authority cell partial on a UX affordance would mis-state where the risk is.
conditionsOnTheJudgement: Track Q1 (typed AUTH_REJECTED/'membership-revoked' close for an already-bound socket, needing a participant-keyed socket index in bindCampaignSyncConnection, whose socketsByMatch is keyed by matchId only) as its OWN item - a product/UX decision for the parent, not a blocker on this cell.

DECLARE the scope boundary in whatever marks the cell: this slice closes SEAT revocation on the session's live surface. The GRANT delivery channel is a different subsystem (handleCampaignGrantJoin.ts, which contains zero attachLiveParticipant calls, with its own revocation under task 4.3); it was neither changed nor measured here. If the cell's owner reads 'revocation' as spanning the grant channel too, THAT half needs its own evidence and this review takes no position on it.
The cell's other elements (append, restart, catch-up, redaction) are carried by CO3 and the privacy rows, not by this slice.

nonClaimsOfThisReview: I did not re-run mutants c or d; I verified their log hashes and, for c, verified the survival MECHANISM at source (CampaignMatchHost.ts:262-266).
I ran the privacy spec ONCE, as briefed. The lane's second privacy run and its CO3 convergence regression run were not reproduced by me; their log hashes match their declared values.
I did not run the full test suite, the full lint, or npm run build:prod - only the brief's scoped gates.

I did not push, commit, rebase, or open a PR, and I changed no tracked file: the two mutants were reverted with git checkout -- and the working tree is clean at both the file-hash and git-status level.
I take no position on whether the GRANT delivery channel (task 4.3) closes for a seat-revoked participant; it is outside this slice and was not measured.
Finding F1's hazard is argued from code reading plus a reachability audit, not from a failing row - by construction it cannot have one while the revocation gate holds.
